title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
A Tesla vehicle operating on Autopilot was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family of the deceased that the vehicle's crash data had been deleted and was unavailable. A hacker later demonstrated that the data had been retained on the vehicle, contradicting Tesla's account to the family.

This is a failure of transparency in a safety-critical system. Tesla had the information needed to understand what happened but did not provide it when asked, even though the data remained accessible. A jury ordered Tesla to pay more than $240 million in the case. A judge later upheld the verdict. It is not established from these reports what specific features of Autopilot were active at the time of the crash or what the recovered data showed about the system's behavior.
